**[1] `virtualization.hypervisor.id`:** A UUID or other platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this hypervisor instance within the virtualization platform.

**[2] `virtualization.hypervisor.type`:** Classifies the hypervisor by its position in the virtualization stack. Type-1 (bare-metal) hypervisors run directly on hardware; Type-2 (hosted) hypervisors run within a host operating system.

**[3] `virtualization.hypervisor.version`:** The version as reported by the hypervisor software itself. Format is hypervisor-specific and should be used for informational purposes and correlation with vendor release notes.

**[4] `virtualization.partition.cpu.type`:** On IBM Z PR/SM (Processor Resource/Systems Manager) partitions, processor resources are differentiated by specialisation purpose. A partition may receive allocations of different processor types simultaneously. Use `all` to report aggregate utilization or count across all types. On hypervisors that do not differentiate processor types, omit this attribute or use `unknown`.

**[5] `virtualization.partition.id`:** A platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this partition within its virtualization platform. On IBM Z in PR/SM (classic) mode this is the partition object-id assigned by the HMC.

**[6] `virtualization.partition.name`:** The name as configured in the hypervisor management interface, e.g., the HMC (Hardware Management Console) for IBM Z PR/SM partitions. On IBM Z, partition names are 1–8 uppercase alphanumeric characters.

**[7] `virtualization.partition.number`:** The numeric index identifying the partition within the platform. On IBM Z PR/SM (classic) mode, this corresponds to the LPAR number as reported by the HMC Web Services API.

**[8] `virtualization.partition.state`:** Reflects the current activation or execution state of the partition as reported by the virtualization platform management interface.

**[9] `virtualization.partition.type`:** Classifies the partition by the category of workload it is configured to run. On IBM Z, this maps to the partition type field on the HMC.

**[10] `virtualization.platform.firmware.version`:** The firmware or microcode version as reported by the platform management interface. For IBM Z this corresponds to the driver or MCL level reported by the HMC. No equivalent exists in the upstream OTel base registry; this attribute is specific to the virtualization schema.

**[11] `virtualization.platform.id`:** A platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this physical computing platform within its management domain. For IBM Z this corresponds to the CPC (Central Processing Complex) object-id as reported by the HMC Web Services API. Alignment with OTel base registry: this attribute is functionally equivalent to `host.id`. Consumers that understand the generic host entity should prefer `host.id`; use this attribute when the management domain requires the platform-internal UUID specifically. In virtualization.platform metrics, `virtualization.platform.id` is used as the time-series discriminating attribute because the identity attribute of the `virtualization.platform` entity is `host.name` and the UUID is needed to uniquely identify the entity instance when metrics are aggregated across platforms with different name scopes.

**[12] `virtualization.platform.model`:** Identifies the hardware model of the physical platform. For IBM Z systems this is the machine type and model concatenated with a hyphen, e.g., "9175-ME1" for the IBM z16 Model ME1. Alignment with OTel base registry: this attribute is equivalent to `host.type`. The `virtualization.platform` entity uses `host.type` in its description; this attribute is retained for implementations that also populate the platform-specific model string separately or for consumers that expect the virtualization namespace naming.

**[13] `virtualization.platform.name`:** The name as configured in the platform management interface. For IBM Z this is the CPC name as configured on the Hardware Management Console (HMC). Alignment with OTel base registry: this attribute is equivalent to `host.name`. The `virtualization.platform` entity uses `host.name` as its identity attribute; this attribute is retained for implementations that also populate the platform-specific name separately or for consumers that expect the virtualization namespace naming.

**[14] `virtualization.platform.serial_number`:** The hardware serial number as reported by the platform management interface. Used to uniquely identify a physical system when multiple systems share the same model or name. Alignment with OTel base registry: the base registry does not have a dedicated serial-number attribute. The closest upstream attribute is `host.id`, which carries an opaque hardware UUID. For IBM Z, the CPC serial number supplements `host.id` (the object-id UUID); both should be populated when available.

**[15] `virtualization.platform.vm.state`:** Used as a discriminating dimension on the `virtualization.platform.vm.count` metric to report counts broken down by VM power state. Use `all` to report the total count across all states. Implementations may omit this attribute and report only the total count when per-state breakdown is not available.

**[16] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the specific hypervisor or partitioning technology in use. This attribute allows consumers to correlate platform-specific behaviour and capabilities when multiple virtualization technologies are observed in a mixed environment. No equivalent exists in the upstream OTel base registry; this attribute is specific to the virtualization schema.

**[17] `virtualization.vm.cpu.count`:** The number of virtual CPUs visible to the guest operating system. This may differ from the number of physical CPUs on the underlying host.

**[18] `virtualization.vm.disk.name`:** The disk name as reported by the hypervisor management API. Used to attribute per-disk I/O metrics to a specific virtual disk when a VM has multiple disks attached. For IBM Z DPM partitions this corresponds to the storage volume name; for VMware ESXi it is the datastore path; for Microsoft Hyper-V it is the virtual hard disk file name.

**[19] `virtualization.vm.id`:** A UUID or other platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this virtual machine within the hypervisor. Analogous to `host.id` for physical machines or a container ID for containers.

**[20] `virtualization.vm.instance_id`:** A provider-assigned instance identifier, distinct from the hypervisor's own identifier (`virtualization.vm.id`). For example, on AWS this would be the EC2 instance ID; on IBM Z HMC DPM mode it would be the partition object-id.

**[21] `virtualization.vm.machine_type`:** A string identifying the virtual machine's hardware configuration class as defined by the hypervisor or cloud provider. For IBM Z DPM partitions this corresponds to the partition type profile.

**[22] `virtualization.vm.memory.size`:** The total memory allocation visible to the guest operating system, expressed in mebibytes (MiB). This is the configured allocation, not necessarily the currently consumed amount.

**[23] `virtualization.vm.name`:** The name as configured in the hypervisor management interface. Names are not guaranteed to be unique across hypervisors; use `virtualization.vm.id` for unambiguous identification.

**[24] `virtualization.vm.nested_virtualization.enabled`:** When `true`, the virtual machine is configured to expose virtualization extensions to its guest operating system, allowing a hypervisor to run inside the VM. Not all hypervisors or platforms support this capability.

**[25] `virtualization.vm.network.interface.name`:** The interface name as reported by the hypervisor management API. Used to attribute per-NIC throughput metrics when a VM has multiple virtual network interfaces. For IBM Z DPM partitions this corresponds to the NIC object name reported by the HMC Web Services API; for VMware ESXi it is the network adapter label; for Microsoft Hyper-V it is the virtual network adapter name.

**[26] `virtualization.vm.node.name`:** In KVM-based environments managed by Kubernetes such as OpenShift Virtualization (KubeVirt), a virtual machine instance (VMI) runs as a pod on a Kubernetes node. This attribute corresponds to the Kubernetes node name (spec.nodeName on the VMI pod) and is equivalent to `k8s.node.name` for standard workloads. It is used to correlate VM performance with the physical host's resource availability. In standalone KVM environments managed by libvirt, this corresponds to the hypervisor hostname. Not applicable on IBM Z PR/SM or cloud hypervisors where VM placement is opaque to the consumer.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | Hypervisor is running and managing virtual machines. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `inactive` | Hypervisor is not currently running. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `unknown` | Hypervisor state is not known. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

`virtualization.vm.state` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `failed` | Virtual machine has encountered a fatal error and cannot recover without operator intervention. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `migrating` | Virtual machine is being live-migrated to another host without interruption. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `paused` | Virtual machine is suspended with state preserved in memory. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `running` | Virtual machine is running and processing workloads. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `scheduled` | Virtual machine has been assigned to a host node and is being prepared to start. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `scheduling` | Virtual machine has been requested but is waiting for the scheduler to assign it to a host node. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `stopped` | Virtual machine is stopped and not consuming CPU resources. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `succeeded` | Virtual machine completed its workload and terminated cleanly (applicable to batch or ephemeral VMs). | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
